subject: Renewal: slice rebalancing + short-term GPU top-up guidance
messages:
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@helix.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixAI Billing <billing@helix.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — capacity top-up + short burst pool

Hi Avery,

We reviewed our October usage and saw a persistent 38% uplift in inference tokens for our recommendation pipeline. The committed GPUs under the current renewal (HX-2026-457) are hitting sustained 85-92% utilization in peak windows, and tail latency spikes are impacting some of our A/B experiment traffic.

Before we sign the renewal, the product team is asking if we can propose a short-term top-up (3 months) and a gradual slice rebalance to remove the peaks without increasing our long-term commit too much. Specifically: can Redwood provide a 10–15% short-term bump (preferably as burst capacity) and an operational plan that shows how we’d reallocate existing tranche slices to smooth utilization across windows?

Attaching our Q3 utilization export.

Appreciate a proposal we can share internally by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Wilson
Head of Platform Engineering, HelixAI
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@helix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, HelixAI Billing <billing@helix.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T13:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity top-up + short burst pool

Hi Sam — thanks for the data and the ask. We can absolutely support a short-term top-up and deliver a slice-rebalancing plan that preserves your long-term commit profile. High level proposal (will expand in an SOW draft):

- Short-term burst: +12% GPU capacity for 90 days, provisioned as a burst pool that sits behind your existing tranche and only routes overflow traffic to avoid changing token billing for steady-state traffic.
- Slice rebalance: reassign 2 tranche slices from underused windows to peak slots, plus KV prefix caching tweaks to reduce repeated context re-computation (expected ~6–9% per-token decrease in peak windows).
- Fallbacks: automatic rollback to baseline if tail latencies exceed agreed SLOs after change.
- Timeline: we can stand up the burst pool within 7 business days after DocuSign on the top-up amendment.

Ben — can you validate the feasibility of the burst pool config and whether we should recommend A100s vs H100s for the burst? I’m tagging Kimberly to draft pricing options (90d) and a small SOW addendum.

Sam — attached is a one-page outline. We’ll follow up with detailed tranche math and a draft amendment by Tuesday EOD.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Dedicated / Enterprise, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-07T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity top-up + short burst pool

Quick technical check from infra: proposed approach looks sound. Notes and recommendations: 

- Burst hardware: recommend mixing 12x H100-style instances (for low-latency tail handling) + 6x A100-style (for throughput-heavy batch jobs). That hybrid reduces cost while tackling tail spikes.
- Kernel packing: we’ll enable kernel-consolidation for the burst pool to co-locate smaller chat workloads and reduce per-token overhead. Expect ~10–12% tail latency reduction top end.
- Quantization profile: apply the same 4-bit fast path used in your prod variants; we’ll run a short canary to confirm model quality loss is within the acceptable regression window.
- Routing policy: set policy to route requests exceeding a 95th percentile latency threshold to the burst pool for up to 3s of additional processing; anything longer will fallback to baseline model for resiliency.

Operational risks: a) cold-start cache misses on burst nodes for first 30–60 minutes (mitigated via pre-warming), b) cross-node KV cache invalidation — we’ll adopt sticky prefixes during the transition.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the CS/ops teams and a canary checklist.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
